chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: A local pianist who embellished popular songs
summary: Randolph recalls a pianist (Benton Overstreet, he thinks) who improvised ornaments on popular songs.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, back home beforeyou went to college, did you try playing any ragtime on the trumpet, or any musicians around there who wanted to play ragtime?

No, there wasn't any. I had one fellow around there. He played, but he played piano and he was doing -- what was he doing? Da-da-da-da -- Benton Overstreet, I think. Did you know -- did you ever hear of Benton Overstreet? I think Overstreet wrote that.
Yeah, but he was just playing popular songs -- this piano player?
Yeah, he was just playing popular songs on it. But he was adding a whole lot -- he'd done a lot of improvising.
Figurations, as the ragtime players would say.

Yes, he certainly was. A lot of ornaments and decorations and everything. And he was really making it sound good, because I know -- I spoke to a young lady and I said, "I don't like such and such a number," and she'd say, "Say, you haven't heard --," I've forgotten the fellow's name now. She said, anyway, I'll just say John. She said, "You haven't heard John play it." So, I finally got a chance to hear the wrote (or co-wrote) 'Dixie' by James Bland
John play it and it didn't sound like it did when --
So, he was doing some improvising or (unintelligible) some configurations in there.
